captions.detailed: A 3D model of a cross-slide milling vise. It features a dark grey rectangular base, an intermediate X-slide that translates along the lower axis, and a top Y-slide carrying two parallel clamping jaws. Two black circular handwheels with small crank handles control the movement: one extends from the front for the X-axis translation, and the other extends from the side for the Y-axis translation. The slides translate prismatically in perpendicular horizontal directions, while the crank handwheels rotate continuously on their shafts.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a cross-slide milling vise with a dark grey base, a middle slide, and a top slide with clamping jaws. Include two continuous-rotation black handwheels mounted on cylindrical lead-screw shafts to control the perpendicular prismatic translation of the slides.
captions.factory: Construct the base plate using a Box primitive. Build the intermediate X-slide and the top Y-slide using stacked and offset Box primitives to represent the guide rails and jaw plates. Model the lead-screw shafts and handwheels using Cylinder primitives for the rods, wheels, and crank handles. Define prismatic joints between the base and the X-slide, and between the X-slide and the Y-slide, while defining continuous revolute joints for the two handwheels.
